request: Please find me data regarding first-of-class ship cost overruns

reply.reply:
**CRS examples show different first-of-class cost pressures: Ford CVN-78’s final procurement cost was $13,316.5 million; the FFG-62 lead ship estimate was $1,499.3 million, and subsequent reported design-weight growth indicated potential cost growth.**

- In October 2023, the FFG-62 shipbuilder reported unplanned design weight growth of over 10 percent versus its June 2020 estimate, suggesting potential cost growth. (R44972, PDF p. 39)
- The lead ship estimate was $1,499.3 million, higher than follow-on ships due to the learning curve and inclusion of much of the class design and nonrecurring engineering costs. (R44972, PDF p. 10)
- The lead Ford-class carrier CVN-78 was procured in FY2008 and had a final procurement cost of $13,316.5 million in then-year dollars. (RS20643, PDF p. 7)
reply.reasoning: Current CRS coverage provides Ford CVN-78’s final procurement cost and an FFG-62 lead-ship estimate alongside a reported weight increase associated with potential cost growth. The available passages do not establish directly comparable overrun percentages.
